Container.Name: github-runner
Container.Overview:
Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner, one instance per repository. Minutes on a self-hosted runner do not count against the account's Actions allowance, which is the reason to run one: a repository whose CI runs a full test suite against a real database service container is what consumes that allowance. The template itself names no repository and no host — set ACCESS_TOKEN, REPO_URL, RUNNER_NAME and LABELS per instance. The runner registers on start and appears under the repository's Settings -> Actions -> Runners; a workflow selects it with runs-on: [self-hosted, <your label>].
TWO THINGS ARE EASY TO GET WRONG.
(1) NETWORK MODE. The default of host is deliberate. This container drives the host's Docker daemon through the mounted socket, so a service container declared by a workflow is created by that daemon and is NOT in this container's network namespace. On bridge, a workflow written the GitHub-hosted way — talking to its service on localhost — cannot reach it there, even though the service is running and healthy; it is reachable via the docker bridge gateway, but only after a workflow change. host makes localhost mean the same thing it means on a GitHub-hosted runner, so existing workflows keep working unchanged. Note also that a service is only published to a host port if the workflow asks: a bare `ports: - 5432` takes a RANDOM host port (read it from job.services.<id>.ports), and a fixed localhost:5432 needs `ports: - 5432:5432`. The cost of host mode is that workflow steps share the host's loopback, so a job can reach anything bound to 127.0.0.1 on the host, including the Unraid webGUI, that a bridge container could not.
(2) SECURITY. The Docker socket mount gives a workflow control of the host's daemon, which is host root, and any job can also read this container's own environment (including ACCESS_TOKEN). Nothing here is a containment boundary and EPHEMERAL does not make one. Run only repositories whose workflow code you control, and do not point a runner at a public repository where a fork pull request can run attacker-authored workflow code.
One runner executes ONE job at a time. For concurrency add a second instance with its own Name, its own RUNNER_NAME, and — if you use the optional work directory — its own directory pair.
Container.Description: Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner (neutral template, one instance per repository). Set the PAT, repository URL, runner name and labels at creation. Network mode host is deliberate; see the Overview.

Config.Name: Docker socket
Config.Description: Required for any workflow that builds an image, declares a services: container, or uses an action that shells out to docker (build-push-action, buildx, testcontainers). It grants this container control of the host's Docker daemon, which is equivalent to root on the host: a workflow that runs here can start any container, mount any host path, and read this container's own environment. Mount it only for repositories whose workflow code you control.

Config.Name: ACCESS_TOKEN
Config.Description: GitHub Personal Access Token used to mint short-lived runner registration tokens. Fine-grained, scoped to this ONE repository, with Administration: read and write (the permission that mints a registration token) — not a classic token with blanket repo scope. It is used at START to register and again at STOP to deregister, so rotating it while a container is running leaves that runner unable to deregister and a stale offline entry on the repository's runner page; rotate and restart while the old token still works. With EPHEMERAL set it is used on every job, not only at restart. TREAT IT AS EXPOSED TO YOUR WORKFLOWS: Mask hides it in this UI only, Unraid stores it in plain text in the container's template on the flash drive, and any job on this runner can read it from its own environment. A compromised workflow is a compromised PAT.

Config.Name: REPO_URL
Config.Description: Full URL of the repository this runner serves: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> . This template is repository-scoped only (see RUNNER_SCOPE), so this is always a repository URL.

Config.Name: RUNNER_NAME
Config.Description: The name this runner registers under, e.g. <repo>-runner-1. It appears in the repository's runner list AND in the job log of every workflow run — on a PUBLIC repository those logs are world-readable, so pick a name that reveals nothing about the machine. Must be unique: the runner registers with --replace, so a second instance sharing a name does NOT error, it silently takes over the first one's registration and the two then fight over one identity.

Config.Name: LABELS
Config.Description: Comma-separated labels a workflow selects this runner by. The runner also adds self-hosted, Linux and X64 itself (unless registered with NO_DEFAULT_LABELS, which this template does not expose), and once registered those cannot be deleted from its page. So the shipped default of self-hosted is a placeholder that adds nothing: a bare runs-on: self-hosted already reaches every runner available to that repository. CHANGE IT before you have a second runner — give each one a distinguishing label, e.g. self-hosted,<repo>, and target runs-on: [self-hosted, <that label>]. Labels appear in public workflow logs, so keep them neutral.

Config.Name: RUNNER_SCOPE
Config.Description: Leave at repo. The image also accepts org and ent, but those modes ignore REPO_URL and read ORG_NAME / ENTERPRISE_NAME instead, and this template deliberately exposes neither — setting org or ent here produces a confusing registration failure rather than a clear error. An org-wide runner also accepts jobs from every repository in the org, so it is only as trustworthy as the least trustworthy workflow there.

Config.Name: RUNNER_WORKDIR
Config.Description: Where the runner checks code out INSIDE this container. Leave as-is unless you are also setting the optional work directory mount below, in which case the two must agree and each runner on the host needs its own.

Config.Name: Work directory (optional)
Config.Description: OPTIONAL, normally left EMPTY. Set it only to run jobs inside a job container (the workflow container: key), which needs the same workspace path to exist on the host and in this container. Then the host path and the container path MUST be the identical string, with RUNNER_WORKDIR inside it. RUNNERS ON ONE HOST MUST NEVER SHARE A WORK DIRECTORY — give each its own trio (container /tmp/runner-1, host <persistent path>/runner-1, RUNNER_WORKDIR /tmp/runner-1/work) or concurrent jobs corrupt each other's checkouts. On Unraid /tmp is RAM-backed, so point the HOST side at persistent storage, not at the host's own /tmp. A path mismatch does not raise a clear error; it usually surfaces as file-not-found failures inside the job container.

Config.Name: EPHEMERAL
Config.Description: OPTIONAL. Set to true to accept exactly ONE job and then deregister; it needs a restart policy that brings the container back, or the runner disappears after one job. What does NOT carry over is the registration. What DOES carry over: this container's filesystem if the same container restarts, any mounted work directory, and every image, volume and build-cache entry the job created on the host daemon. It is not a containment boundary — with the Docker socket mounted a job is host root either way — so it is not what makes running untrusted or fork-pull-request code safe. Nothing here is.
